questions.prompt: Did the envoy, driven from the camp, confess the truth?
questions.answer: Cōnfessusne est lēgātus ē castrīs pulsus vēritātem?

questions.prompt: Does the field abound in cucumbers and sown crops this year?
questions.answer: Abundatne ager cucumeribus satīsque hōc annō?

questions.prompt: Are you climbing the steep ridge, leaning on your spear?
questions.answer: Ascendisne iugum arduum hastā innīxus?

questions.prompt: Surely you desire to return to your native shore?
questions.answer: Nōnne cupis ad lītus patrium redīre?

questions.prompt: Surely the leader saw the hidden movement of the enemy?
questions.answer: Nōnne dux mōtum hostium occultum vīdit?

questions.prompt: Surely those crops, watered by rain, will profit the farmer?
questions.answer: Nōnne sata imbre rigāta agricolae prōfutūra sunt?

questions.prompt: Surely you pour a libation to the gods before the battle?
questions.answer: Nōnne dīs ante proelium lībās?

questions.prompt: You aren't afraid of the prisoner's false confession, are you?
questions.answer: Num falsam captīvī cōnfessiōnem timēs?

questions.prompt: The soldiers weren't driven back from the wall, were they?
questions.answer: Num mīlitēs ā mūrō pulsī sunt?

questions.prompt: The rack didn't wring the truth from the innocent man, did it?
questions.answer: Num equuleus vēritātem ab īnsonte expressit?

questions.prompt: You don't long for war, now that peace has been made, do you?
questions.answer: Num bellī dēsīderium habēs pāce factā?

questions.prompt: Why did the envoy, sent by the king, enter the hostile camp?
questions.answer: Cūr lēgātus ā rēge missus castra hostīlia iniit?

questions.prompt: How many ships did the enemy drive to our shores by night?
questions.answer: Quot nāvēs hostis ad lītora nostra nocte pepulit?

questions.prompt: When will the ardent young man cease to long for glory?
questions.answer: Quandō iuvenis ardēns glōriam dēsīderāre dēsinet?

questions.prompt: How did the small band drive the enemy from the steep pass?
questions.answer: Quōmodo parva manus hostem saltū arduō expulit?

questions.prompt: What did the boy, leaning on his staff, ask about the war?
questions.answer: Quid puer baculō innīxus dē bellō rogāvit?

questions.prompt: You do see the crops abounding in the wide fields, don't you?
questions.answer: Vidēsne sata in campīs lātīs abundāre?

questions.prompt: The false envoy won't be of any use to us, will he?
questions.answer: Num falsus lēgātus nōbīs prōderit?

questions.prompt: I asked how the enemy had crossed the swollen river.
questions.answer: Rogāvī quōmodo hostis flūmen tumidum trānsīsset.

questions.prompt: Do you see the column of soldiers advancing through the valley?
questions.answer: Vidēsne agmen mīlitum per vallem prōgrediēns?

questions.prompt: Surely you know why the general, weary from battle, retreated?
questions.answer: Nōnne scīs cūr dux, proeliō fessus, sē recēperit?

questions.prompt: You aren't afraid of the enemy hidden in the woods, are you?
questions.answer: Num hostem in silvīs latentem timēs?

questions.prompt: The old man asked when the ships would return to the harbor.
questions.answer: Senex rogāvit quandō nāvēs in portum reditūrae essent.

questions.prompt: Who dared to creep across the wall by night?
questions.answer: Quis per mūrum noctū rēpere ausus est?

questions.prompt: Do you understand how the poet arranged the syllables of his verse?
questions.answer: Intellegisne quōmodo poēta syllabās versūs suī dispōsuerit?

questions.prompt: Surely the artist, ignorant of nothing, examined the statue carefully?
questions.answer: Nōnne artifex, nūllīus reī ignārus, statuam dīligenter īnspexit?

questions.prompt: Why does envy make the wicked man's face grow pale?
questions.answer: Cūr līvor vultum improbī pallēscere cōgit?

questions.prompt: Do you know where the guide directed the wandering travelers?
questions.answer: Scīsne ubi dux errantēs viātōrēs dīrēxerit?

questions.prompt: You don't think the ice will refresh the sick soldiers, do you?
questions.answer: Num glaciēs mīlitēs aegrōs refrīgerābit?

questions.prompt: Surely the fresh troops surpassed the enemy in speed?
questions.answer: Nōnne novae cōpiae hostēs celeritāte antecessērunt?

questions.prompt: When did the astonished crowd fall silent before the king?
questions.answer: Quandō turba obstupefacta ante rēgem conticuit?

questions.prompt: Do you provoke the sleeping lion with your reckless words?
questions.answer: Irrītāsne leōnem dormientem verbīs temerāriīs?

questions.prompt: The commander wondered how the scattered ranks had run together again.
questions.answer: Imperātor mīrābātur quōmodo agmina dispersa dēnuō concurrissent.

questions.prompt: Surely you clothed the shivering children in warm garments?
questions.answer: Nōnne puerōs trementēs calidīs vestīmentīs vestīvistī?

questions.prompt: What did the physician inspect while the wound was rotting?
questions.answer: Quid medicus, vulnere tābente, īnspexit?

questions.prompt: Do you know why the boy, equal to no one in skill, was praised?
questions.answer: Scīsne cūr puer, nūllī arte pār, laudātus sit?

questions.prompt: You aren't cutting the rest of the branches, are you?
questions.answer: Num cēterōs rāmōs concīdis?

questions.prompt: How did the torches light up the darkness of the night?
questions.answer: Quōmodo facēs noctis tenebrās lūmināvērunt?

questions.prompt: Surely the snake crept quietly toward the unwary bird?
questions.answer: Nōnne serpēns tacitē ad avem ignāram rēpsit?

questions.prompt: Do you see how the soldiers, drawn up in a line, advance?
questions.answer: Vidēsne quōmodo mīlitēs, in aciē īnstrūctī, prōcēdant?

questions.prompt: Where did the merchants, astonished by the storm, seek refuge?
questions.answer: Ubi mercātōrēs, tempestāte obstupefactī, perfugium petīvērunt?

questions.prompt: The judge asked who had provoked the citizens to anger.
questions.answer: Iūdex rogāvit quis cīvēs ad īram irrītāvisset.

questions.prompt: Surely you admire the general's restraint amid so many dangers?
questions.answer: Nōnne temperantiam ducis inter tot perīcula admīrāris?

questions.prompt: The wandering robber didn't lose his way in the darkness, did he?
questions.answer: Num latrō errāns in tenebrīs viam āmīsit?

questions.prompt: How long will the nimble messenger stay in the enemy's camp?
questions.answer: Quam diū nūntius agilis in castrīs hostium manēbit?

questions.prompt: Is the omen favorable or unfavorable, since the gods keep silent?
questions.answer: Utrum ōmen faustum an īnfaustum est, cum diī taceant?

questions.prompt: Do you perceive how effectively the leader corrected the citizens' error?
questions.answer: Sentīsne quam efficāciter dux cīvium errōrem corrēxerit?

questions.prompt: Surely the divine poet, crowned with laurel, deserved such honor?
questions.answer: Nōnne poēta dīvus, laurō corōnātus, tantum honōrem meruit?

questions.prompt: How often did the tardy guest disturb the sacred rites?
questions.answer: Quotiēns hospes tardus sacra turbāvit?

questions.prompt: You don't suppose both brothers seized the plunder, do you?
questions.answer: Num ambō frātrēs praedam abripuērunt?

questions.prompt: Is malice or ignorance the cause of so great a crime?
questions.answer: Malignitāsne an ignōrantia tantī sceleris causa est?

questions.prompt: Why did the parent entrust the child to so untrustworthy a guardian?
questions.answer: Cūr parēns īnfantem tam īnfīdō custōdī crēdidit?

questions.prompt: Surely the kinsman, moved by affection, freed the wretched captives?
questions.answer: Nōnne cognātus, familiāritāte mōtus, captīvōs miserōs līberāvit?

questions.prompt: Who could endure so great an insult in silence?
questions.answer: Quis tantam contumēliam tacitus ferre possit?

questions.prompt: Do you dare to deny it? Why are you silent? I will convict you, if you deny it. For I see that there are here in the Senate certain men who were together with you.
questions.answer: Num negāre audēs? Quid tacēs? Convincam, sī negās. Videō enim esse hīc in Senātū quōsdam, quī tēcum ūna fuērunt.

questions.prompt: Does he — what matters most — know our laws or customs, does he, in short, know men?
questions.answer: Num, quod maximum est, lēgēs nostrās moresve nōvit, num dēnique hominēs?

questions.prompt: What is it, Catiline? Do you notice at all, do you observe at all the silence of these men? They endure, they are silent. Why do you await the authority of those speaking, whose will, though silent, you perceive?
questions.answer: Quid est, Catilīna? Ecquid attendis, ecquid animadvertis hōrum silentium? Patiuntur, tacent. Quid exspectās auctōritātem loquentium, quōrum voluntātem tacitōrum perspicis?

questions.prompt: What, pray, hinders you? The custom of your ancestors?
questions.answer: Quid tandem tē impedit? Mōsne maiōrum?

questions.prompt: Do you have two fatherlands, or is that one fatherland a common one?
questions.answer: Numquid duās habētis patriās, an est ūna illa patria communis?

questions.prompt: Surely, Catiline, so great, so atrocious, so incredible a matter did not escape me — and, what is far more to be wondered at, the very day?
questions.answer: Num mē fefellit, Catilīna, nōn modo rēs tanta, tam atrōx, tamque incrēdibilis, vērum — id quod multō magis est admīrandum — diēs?

questions.prompt: Or do you fear the ill-will of posterity?
questions.answer: An invidiam posteritātis timēs?

questions.prompt: Does he seem to you to fear death or pain?
questions.answer: Is tibi mortemne vidētur aut dolōrem timēre?

questions.prompt: Do you not see that your schemes are manifest?
questions.answer: Patēre tua cōnsilia nōn sentīs?

questions.prompt: Don't you remember my saying in the Senate?
questions.answer: Meministīne mē in senātū dīcere?

questions.prompt: Do I not rightly interpret your meaning?
questions.answer: Rēctēne interpretor sententiam tuam?

questions.prompt: Whither then is all this tending?
questions.answer: Quō igitur haec spectant?

questions.prompt: What revenue has been safe for you? What ally have you defended? Whom have you guarded with your fleets?
questions.answer: Quod vectīgal vōbīs tūtum fuit? Quem socium dēfendistis? Cui praesidiō classibus vestrīs fuistis?

questions.prompt: In what city, pray, do they maintain this?
questions.answer: In quā tandem urbe hōc disputant?

questions.prompt: Is it that you don't know, or do you think nothing of it?
questions.answer: Utrum nescīs, an prō nihilō id putās?

questions.prompt: Did you desert Lucius Domitius, or did Domitius desert you?
questions.answer: Vōsne L. Domitium an vōs Domitius dēseruit?

questions.prompt: I ask whether slaves or free.
questions.answer: Quaerō servōsne an līberōs.

questions.prompt: Is it the enemy, or yourselves, or the fortune of the two peoples, that you do not know?
questions.answer: Utrum hostem an vōs an fortūnam utrīusque populī īgnōrātis?

questions.prompt: Are these your words or not?
questions.answer: Sunt haec tua verba necne?

questions.prompt: What! Do you think those men wretched?
questions.answer: An tū miserōs putās illōs?

questions.prompt: Would he ever have had good hopes about himself unless he had conceived an evil opinion of you?
questions.answer: An iste umquam dē sē bonam spem habuisset, nisi dē vōbīs malam opīniōnem animō imbibisset?

questions.prompt: Do you despise these things? Not at all.
questions.answer: An haec contemnitis? Minimē.

questions.prompt: To the birds and beasts? Why, of course not.
questions.answer: Volucribusne et ferīs? Minimē vērō.
